front: Je suis infirmière à l'hôpital.
back: I'm a nurse at the hospital.
context: No article before professions with être. Masculine: infirmier.

front: Il est ingénieur dans une entreprise de logiciels.
pronunciation: [eel eh tan-zhay-NYUHR dahn zün ahn-truh-PREEZ duh loh-zhee-SYEL]
back: He's an engineer at a software company.
context: 'Une entreprise' = company. 'Un logiciel' = software.

front: Elle travaille comme avocate.
back: She works as a lawyer.
context: 'Travailler comme' + profession = to work as.

front: Je suis au chômage en ce moment.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee zoh shoh-MAHZH ahn suh moh-MAHN]
back: I'm unemployed at the moment.
context: 'Être au chômage' = to be unemployed. 'Pôle emploi', now 'France Travail', is the job center.

front: Je cherche du travail.
back: I'm looking for work.
context: 'Le travail' = work; 'un emploi', 'un poste' = a job.

front: J'ai un entretien d'embauche demain.
back: I have a job interview tomorrow.
context: 'L'embauche' = hiring; 'embaucher' = to hire.

front: J'ai un CDI.
back: I have a permanent contract.
context: CDI (contrat à durée indéterminée) = permanent job; CDD = fixed-term contract. A CDI matters a lot when renting in France.

front: Je travaille à temps partiel.
back: I work part-time.
context: 'À temps plein' = full-time. The legal full-time week in France is 35 hours.

front: Je fais du télétravail deux jours par semaine.
pronunciation: [zhuh feh dü tay-lay-trah-VAHY duh zhoor par suh-MEN]
back: I work from home two days a week.
context: 'Le télétravail' = remote work.

front: Mon bureau est au cinquième étage.
back: My office is on the fifth floor.
context: 'Le bureau' = office or desk.

front: Je suis en réunion jusqu'à quinze heures.
back: I'm in a meeting until 3 p.m.
context: 'Être en réunion' = to be in a meeting.

front: Mon collègue est en congé maladie.
back: My colleague is on sick leave.
context: 'Un congé' = leave; 'les congés payés' = paid holidays (five weeks a year in France).

front: Je pars en vacances la semaine prochaine.
pronunciation: [zhuh par ahn vah-KAHNS lah suh-men proh-SHEN]
back: I'm going on vacation next week.
context: 'Partir en vacances' = to go on holiday.

front: Le patron veut nous voir.
back: The boss wants to see us.
context: 'Le patron' or 'le chef' (informal); 'le/la responsable', 'le directeur' (more formal).

front: Je dois rendre ce rapport avant vendredi.
pronunciation: [zhuh dwah rahn-druh suh rah-POR ah-vahn vahn-druh-DEE]
back: I have to hand in this report before Friday.
context: 'Devoir' + infinitive = to have to. 'Rendre' = to hand in.

front: Vous pouvez m'envoyer le document par mail ?
pronunciation: [voo poo-vay mahn-vwah-yay luh doh-kü-MAHN par MEL]
back: Can you send me the document by email?
context: 'Un mail' or 'un e-mail' in everyday French; 'un courriel' is the official term, common in Québec.

front: Je vous rappelle dans cinq minutes.
back: I'll call you back in five minutes.
context: 'Rappeler' = to call back.

front: Ne quittez pas, je vous le passe.
pronunciation: [nuh kee-tay PAH, zhuh voo luh PAS]
back: Hold the line, I'll put you through.
context: Phone formula: 'Ne quittez pas' = please hold.

front: C'est de la part de qui ?
back: Who's calling, please?
context: Asked by receptionists on the phone.

front: Je suis débordé en ce moment.
back: I'm swamped right now.
context: 'Débordé' = overwhelmed with work (literally overflowing).

front: On fait une pause café ?
back: Shall we take a coffee break?
context: The coffee machine is a social hub in French offices.

front: Je commence à neuf heures et je finis à dix-huit heures.
pronunciation: [zhuh koh-MAHNS ah nuh-VUHR ay zhuh fee-NEE ah dee-zwee-TUHR]
back: I start at nine and finish at six.
context: The lunch break in France is often an hour or more.

front: Bonne continuation !
back: Keep up the good work! / All the best!
context: Said when parting from someone you won't see for a while.

front: Je vous souhaite une bonne journée.
back: I wish you a good day.
context: Polite formula to end a professional call or meeting.

front: Je suis en stage dans une agence de communication.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee zahn STAHZH dahn zün ah-zhahns duh koh-mü-nee-kah-SYOHN]
back: I'm doing an internship at a communications agency.
context: 'Un stage' = internship; 'un/une stagiaire' = intern.

front: Il a été promu directeur commercial.
back: He was promoted to sales director.
context: 'Être promu' = to be promoted; 'une promotion' = a promotion (also a sale or a graduating class).

front: Elle a démissionné le mois dernier.
back: She resigned last month.
context: 'Démissionner' = to resign; 'être licencié' = to be laid off.

front: Le salaire est de deux mille euros brut par mois.
pronunciation: [luh sah-LEHR eh duh duh meel uh-ROH BRÜT par MWAH]
back: The salary is two thousand euros gross per month.
context: French salaries are given monthly, 'brut' (gross) or 'net' (after deductions).

front: Vous pouvez m'envoyer votre CV ?
back: Can you send me your CV?
context: French CVs are usually one page, often with a photo.

front: Quelles sont vos qualités et vos défauts ?
pronunciation: [kel sohn voh kah-lee-TAY ay voh day-FOH]
back: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
context: A classic interview question. 'Un défaut' = a flaw.

front: Je suis organisé et j'aime travailler en équipe.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee zor-gah-nee-ZAY ay zhem trah-vah-yay ahn nay-KEEP]
back: I'm organized and I like working in a team.
context: 'Travailler en équipe' = teamwork.

front: Madame, Monsieur, je me permets de vous écrire…
pronunciation: [mah-DAM, muh-SYUH, zhuh muh pehr-MEH duh voo zay-KREER]
back: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to you…
context: Standard opening of a formal letter or email to someone whose name you don't know.

front: Bien cordialement.
back: Kind regards.
context: The most common professional email sign-off.

front: Ça marche, je m'en occupe.
back: OK, I'll take care of it.
context: 'S'occuper de' = to take care of. 'Ça marche' = OK, works for me (informal but common at work).

front: On se tutoie ou on se vouvoie ?
pronunciation: [ohn suh tü-TWAH oo ohn suh voo-VWAH]
back: Do we use tu or vous?
context: In many French offices colleagues use tu, but vous is safer with managers and clients.
